headline: No clear difference from natural recovery (evidence exists): no option is shown by evidence to beat natural recovery; continue with natural recovery and monitoring. Evidence exists but shows no clear difference for: bioremediation, low_pressure_flushing. Insufficient evidence to compare with natural recovery for: passive_sorbents, manual_removal, mechanical_removal, vacuum_removal, sediment_relocation, sediment_mixing, low_pressure_heated_flushing, vegetation_cutting. Best allowed options (class B): passive_sorbents, bioremediation, manual_removal.

Sand beaches: the sand-beach data model is not integrated yet (D36), so no persistence forecast is shown; the tier becomes experimental when it is.

solidifiers.secondary_impacts: Added material and waste; limited field evidence

mechanical_removal.secondary_impacts: Sediment loss and habitat damage; excluded on marsh and mudflat

sediment_relocation.secondary_impacts: Redistributes oil; only on exposed beaches

sediment_mixing.secondary_impacts: Can bury or spread oil; not for soft or sensitive habitat

bioremediation.secondary_impacts: Effectiveness depends on nutrients, oxygen and access; limited bioaugmentation evidence (NOAA)

vegetation_cutting.secondary_impacts: Removes biomass and can increase erosion; only where sensitivity is high

inputs.class_rules: E excluded > A benefit > D harm under conditions > B no clear evidence; C natural recovery
inputs.ordering: within a class: lower bound of the 90% benefit interval where it exists (edge loss avoided by year 8 in m, then vegetation cover ratio at year 2, then literature lnRR lower bound; units are never mixed), then the ASSUMED ecological score (higher = lower disturbance first), then name

outputs.headline: No clear difference from natural recovery (evidence exists): no option is shown by evidence to beat natural recovery; continue with natural recovery and monitoring. Evidence exists but shows no clear difference for: bioremediation, low_pressure_flushing. Insufficient evidence to compare with natural recovery for: passive_sorbents, manual_removal, mechanical_removal, vacuum_removal, sediment_relocation, sediment_mixing, low_pressure_heated_flushing, vegetation_cutting. Best allowed options (class B): passive_sorbents, bioremediation, manual_removal.

characterisation.oiling_basis: derived from oil_coverage with ASSUMED breaks (>=70 Heavy, >=40 Moderate, >=20 Light, >0 Very_Light)
characterisation.noaa_oil_category_basis: ASSUMED mapping from the tool's oil category (data/knowledge/tables/noaa_oil_category.csv)

habitat_descriptors.name: fine- to medium-grained sand beach
habitat_descriptors.oil_penetration_depth: about 10-15 cm in fine- to medium-grained sand
habitat_descriptors.burial_risk: rapid: within one day; to about 1 m if oil comes ashore at the start of a depositional period
habitat_descriptors.persistence_driver: not stated for sand beaches (NOAA: among the easiest shorelines to clean; heavy oil is lifted off the lower beach by the rising tide)
